restated: Let f(q,r) be the unique p such that (p,q,r) is a P-position of 3-row Chomp, defined by the Brouwer recurrence; for each fixed r let N(r) be the least q0 >= r such that the sequence f(q,r)-q is periodic for all q >= q0 (if row r has only finitely many P-positions, i.e. f(q,r) < q for all large q, N(r) is instead the least q with f(q,r) < q). Define a priori sequences g,h by g(1)=1, g(r+1)=g(r)(r+2)^(r+1), and h(r)=11+r+sum_{k=2}^{r} g(k)(k+2)^(k+1). Then for every r>=1, N(r) <= r+h(r), with g(r)=prod_{k=1}^{r-1}(k+2)^{k+1}, so N(r) <= 2^{O(r^2 log r)}. The bound is explicit and computable and no quantity on the right is defined by a recursion over the actual rows.
ledger_statement: SHARPER CLOSED FORM: N(r) <= 2^{O(r^2 log r)}. The lcm recursion is LINEAR, not quadratic: q_{r+1} <= q_r (r+2)^{r+1}, because the pigeonhole's repeated state carries the phase a mod q_r, so the repeated-period s satisfies q_r | s AND p_r | s, hence q_{r+1}=lcm(q_r,p_r) | s <= q_r(m_r+1)^{m_r} directly. Define g(1)=1, g(r+1)=g(r)(r+2)^(r+1), h(1)=12, h(r)=1+h(r-1)+g(r)(r+2)^(r+1). Then q_r <= g(r), u_r=N(r)-r <= h(r), so N(r) <= r+h(r) = r+11+r+sum_{k=2}^r g(k)(k+2)^(k+1) with g(r)=prod_{k=1}^{r-1}(k+2)^(k+1), log2 g(r) ~ (r^2/2) log2 r. Improves C0027's 2^{2^{O(r)}} to 2^{O(r^2 log r)}. Sharpening to C*r remains open (discrepancy / C0037 locking question).

verdicts.gap_description: At r=1 the induction invokes h(0), which is undefined (h is only defined for r>=1), and u_0 is never bounded, so the base case u_1 <= h(1) is not actually proved. It is fillable in two lines: row 0 has B_0 = 1 identically, so u_0 = 0, q_1 = 1, m_1 = 2, and (iii) gives u_1 <= 1 + max(1,2) + 1*3^2 = 12 = h(1) (solver confirms u_1 = 2). A second fillable slip: Addendum 2's application says the tail is purely periodic on [a1,infty) with least period p_r, but the suffix argument covers only a1 >= u_r; for a1 < u_r one must apply the periods-group lemma on [u_r, infty), where both p_r- and s-periodicity hold.

verdicts.effectivity_check: Effective. The bound is produced by explicit a priori recursions quoted in the proof: "g(1) = 1, g(r+1) = g(r) (r+2)^{r+1}" and "h(1) = 12, h(r) = 1 + h(r-1) + g(r)(r+2)^{r+1}", giving the closed form h(r) = 11 + r + sum_{k=2}^{r} g(k)(k+2)^{k+1} = 2^{Theta(r^2 log r)}. No quantity on the right is defined via the actual rows (m_r <= r+1 comes from cited C0012; q_r <= g(r) from Lemma A'+B'), and no circular appeal to Byrnes' non-effective periodicity occurs: the pigeonhole itself proves the tail periodicity, so N(r) <= r + h(r) is computable for r = 1000 by a person with the statement alone.
